title: iM Securities sees limited Nvidia downside despite Cisco-like pattern; KOSPI lags Japan and Taiwan on foreign selling and strong won
text:
iM Securities sees limited Nvidia downside despite Cisco-like pattern; KOSPI lags Japan and Taiwan on foreign selling and strong won - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 17일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Finance iM Securities sees limited Nvidia downside despite Cisco-like pattern; KOSPI lags Japan and Taiwan on foreign selling and strong won 
 iM Securities says Nvidia's earnings should remain resilient after Jensen Huang's exit, though GPU-backed circular financing poses a key risk to the AI credit cycle 
 입력 2026.11.16. 09:00 업데이트   2026.11.16. 09:02 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Huang Jensen, former Nvidia CEO /Courtesy of Reuters-Yonhap iM Securities said on the 16th that Nvidia's stock has been tracking a pattern similar to Cisco Systems during the dot-com bubble, but it sees little chance that Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO will severely disrupt Nvidia's earnings or trigger another steep plunge in the share price. It added, however, that if financing backed by Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) runs into trouble, it could weigh on investment and credit across the broader artificial intelligence (AI) industry.
 Park Sang-hyun, a researcher at iM Securities, said uncertainty surrounding former CEO Huang's resignation, coupled with questions about AI investment profitability, is making Nvidia's stock trajectory resemble Cisco's during the dot-com era.
 "For now, the risk of a replay of the dot-com bubble is very low," he said. "Nvidia's management activity could slow somewhat without Jensen Huang, but we do not expect its operating results to be badly shaken."
 Park focused on the "circular financing" built around Nvidia. He said the key question after the former CEO's resignation is whether guarantees for startup cloud companies that raise funds with GPUs as collateral will continue without disruption. "If circular financing backed by GPUs hits snags, it will significantly hurt the AI investment cycle and AI-driven credit risk," he said.
 He also cited additional rate hikes by the U.S. Federal Reserve (Fed) as a variable. Because high rates persisted for a considerable period when the dot-com bubble burst, whether the Fed raises rates again next year and by how much could affect AI companies' shares and financing conditions, he said. Even so, credit default swap (CDS) indicators of large cloud firms' credit risk have been largely stable after the Nvidia episode. In the near term, he said he will watch whether Nvidia's earnings this week spark a rebound in the stock.
 ◇ KOSPI's drop in the second half outpaced Japan and Taiwan
 Park also noted that the KOSPI fell more than the Japanese and Taiwanese markets. As of the 13th, the KOSPI was down 37.6% from the end of June, according to the report. Over the same period, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 12.7% and Taiwan's Taiex declined 5.3%.
 The KOSPI's steeper climb in the first half and stronger foreign selling in Korea in the second half widened the decline. "It's clear the usual link—foreign investors increasing their Korea equity exposure when the won strengthens—has weakened," Park said. "The won's relative strength may have created favorable conditions for foreigners to take profits." He also said the stronger won likely weighed on exporters' won-denominated earnings.
 "In the end, fundamentals matter most," Park said. "If Nvidia's operations hold up despite the absence of CEO Jensen Huang and Korea's semiconductor exports maintain strong momentum, the two uncomfortable charts—Nvidia and the KOSPI—will start to show a new trend."
